questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience veterinary medicine as far away from Denmark as possible! Also, I'm curious about grass based dairy- and beef operations, and knew I would be able to learn more about these down under.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a very good trip and some excellent clinical placements. Learned a lot, met a bunch of very wonderful people, and feel much closer to actually being a veterinarian now than before I left.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had no idea what the professional part/placement content would be - there was no way to find out about that. I just crossed my fingers that the teaching would be good with a high caseload. As goes the practical stuff (dormitory, Q-fever vaccination etc.) it was very easy to read up on via Uni Sydney's portals.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: One member of the clinical secretory lend me some "personal assistance" - I could write her with my questions. She helped receiving a parcel of overalls that were required for the courses, and helped me with other practical aspects.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Could have used an access card, which I never received due to IT-problems at the university. However, it worked out fine with my costudents coming to let me in the buildings when I needed it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Local dormitory - "Nepean Hall".

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I rented a box of kitchen gear via the dorm, and the dorm supplied stoves, ovens, and a little fridge+freezer space. I used the dorm shuttle bus to get to the nearest town (Camden) to go grocery shopping.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's fine and there's a gym:) No luxury, nice surroundings for a walk/run

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Was send an email with a registration form which I printed out and filled in and returned to the uni.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administration staff could be contacted if needed

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% - I got to mix and match the placements that I wanted just the way I wanted to!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just choose whatever you like, all the placements I took were incredible

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical level was very high. My costudents were very skilled and there was usually only 1-2 students per teaching vet per case. Lots of hands on, lots of feedback from teaching vets, high expectations to the students and lots of interesting cases. I learned and developed a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more hands-on on livestock placements and more vets per students. More realistic cases, as the cases were "real life" on farm cases and acute cases in the vicinity of the clinic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Livestock Placement x 2
Wildlife Placement x 2

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both the courses I took. Because of the level of hands-on and excellent staffing level.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Great gym
Nice surroundings for a walk/run
Basket/tennis course

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend the gym - and going weekend hiking in the area (Blue Mountains, Coastal Track etc.)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sydney, hiking track in the area (Blue Mountains, Coastal Track etc.), drive down the Sapphire Coast, go surfing in Manly

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I felt like I fit right in with both Aussie and foreign students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be social...? Talk to your costudents, be a part of the group

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to fit in - easier than in Denmark I think. Don't see any particular cultural differences that were challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They outgoingness of my costudents, they weren't afraid to let a foreigner into their social circles

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Do it! The professional and social environment is a treat.
- Make sure to experience the country before/after the placement as well. Such a beautiful country
- Practicalities (living, food, transport) is easy. I don't think you need a car

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write older students who has been on USYD clinical placements if there's anything you're unsure about.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Probably the professional part - the clinical teaching was very ambitious and I learned a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was some long days, sometimes 6-6 clinical days with need of writing records afterwards - set in a setting where the IT record systems, language, culture etc. is foreign, I was sometimes really tired and just needed to relax and wind down in the weekend.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: ABsolutely loved my stay at USYD - it will be a memory of a lifetime.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
